points.description: States that the frequency of light is proportional to its energy (E = hν), so a higher frequency means a photon with more energy.
points.partial_credit: Mentions that energy relates to frequency without stating the proportionality, or states it with a minor error.

points.description: States that the energy levels of an electron in an atom are quantized, and that only a photon whose energy exactly equals the gap between two levels can be absorbed for excitation (so only certain frequencies are absorbed).
points.partial_credit: States quantized levels but does not link absorbed energy to the difference between two levels (1 mark), or links them vaguely.

points.description: States that a minimum energy (threshold frequency) is needed to eject the electron from the atom, and that any energy above this threshold is given to the ejected electron as kinetic energy.
points.partial_credit: States the threshold idea only (1.5 marks) without explaining that the excess energy becomes kinetic energy, or vice versa.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three points: frequency proportional to energy, quantized energy levels with absorption equal to the level gap (so only certain frequencies work for excitation), and a threshold energy for ejection with any excess becoming kinetic energy of the electron. Give part marks where an idea is stated halfway or vaguely, as shown in the partial credit column. A student who only describes the photoelectric effect or restates the question without these links earns no marks for that point.
